what: A31 structure-space counting pilot: size of the PRUNED contact-structure space for the structure-first exclusion campaign at s0 = 3.8771
object: SUPPORT graph H on a loaded core of k squares + 4 wall nodes, counted up to S_k x D4 (exact orbit counts)

ablation_rows.meaning: no filter (simple graphs, k squares + 4 walls, no wall-wall edges)
+ L5(b)  wall-degree <= 2 and the two walls adjacent
+ L1     every loaded square has degree >= 2
+ L3     no floating component (self-stress branch split off)
+ L6     some H-component joins two opposite walls (lam0=0 branch split off)
+ L4(b)  full planarity of H + wall 4-cycle
+ L7     (implied by L6 here; see gap G1)

validation: k=2 and k=3: FULL independent brute force over every edge subset with an independent filter implementation - all 8 ablation rows and all 5 branch counts agree exactly
k=4: independent brute force from the L1 stage on - all rows agree exactly
Burnside orbit formula for R0/R2 agrees with the brute-force orbit count at k=2,3
Level-1 exact decoration count agrees with an independent brute-force enumeration + explicit tilt-ladder search on 24 small cases
Level-1b Monte Carlo reproduces the exact Level-1 tilt acceptance rate within sampling error on every graph tested

SOUNDNESS: the contact graph of Trump's known optimum (s = 3.877084, k = 11 loaded squares, 14 square-square + 11 square-wall edges) passes EVERY hard filter (code/check_trump.py). Its per-wall degrees are 3/3/3/2, exactly meeting the certified per-wall cap of 3 derived here, and its minimum total degree is 3, so it is NOT in the L2 thin branch. Its |E| = 25 is far below the Maxwell threshold 3k+1 = 34, confirming that flush/multi-row contacts carry the rigidity and that |E| >= 3k+1 must NOT be applied as a prune.

gaps.text: The object enumerated is the SUPPORT graph H (positive multipliers), because L1, L3 and L6 are statements about H. L7 is a statement about the ACTIVE-CONTACT graph G, so it is NOT a legitimate hard filter on H and is only reported as a column. In the lambda0>0 branch L6 already implies it, and empirically R10 = R9 at every k, so nothing is lost - but a future enumerator that works on G must not double-use it.

L4 planarity is applied to H together with the wall 4-cycle, exactly as L4's drawing constructs it. If one only accepts planarity of H alone the filter is about 2x weaker (measured: see marginal_kill_on_metric_consistent_set, L4b_graph_only vs L4b_with_wall_cycle). Both counts are reported; MAIN uses the wall-cycle version.

L5(a) is implemented as a relaxation: certified centre boxes from wall membership (x in [1/2, sqrt2/2] on a wall, [s-sqrt2/2, s-1/2] on the far wall, s in [3.80, 3.8771]), the universal centre separation >= 1 for interior-disjoint unit squares, and the chain bound |c_i-c_j| <= sqrt2 * hop-distance. No triangle closure, no full distance-geometry feasibility, no tilt information. It can only ADMIT unrealizable graphs, never reject realizable ones. The 3.80 endpoint uses the certified lower bound s(11) >= 3.80 (A06/A07/A08); with only Stromquist (3.7889) the filter weakens slightly.

The core has EXACTLY k loaded squares; the other 11-k are rattlers / unloaded (L3 case i). The completion multiplicity (ways to park 11-k rattlers) is NOT counted, so the projected totals are PER CORE and the true structure count is larger.

L2 degree-2 thin branches are kept and flagged. They are ~90% of all survivors (k=7: 753767 of 842398), so if L2 collinearity is ever upgraded to a hard prune the space shrinks by roughly one order of magnitude.

The L3 self-stress branch and the lambda0=0 branch are counted SEPARATELY and are not part of MAIN. The lambda0=0 branch is large (k=7: 401250, ~48% of MAIN) and needs its own excludable row system, as drain_lemma requires.

The Maxwell count m >= 3k+1 in its CERTAIN form (all contacts point contacts, m = |E|) is satisfied by ZERO survivors at every k: planarity caps |E| at 3k+2 and no survivor reaches 3k+1. So every candidate needs flush contacts (2 rows each). If Maxwell is ever proved necessary it becomes a very strong filter, forcing at least 3k+1-|E| flush edges; it is NOT applied here (the ledger marks it soft).

Level 1 checks the TILT subsystem only, and does so exactly (equalities mod 90 by union-find, a zero class from wall-flush, strict inequalities from corner-on-edge, feasible iff the class digraph is acyclic and nothing sits below phi=0). Positions are never checked: whether the touching corner actually lands inside the unit edge, non-overlap of non-adjacent squares, and containment are all ignored. The Level-1 fan-out is therefore an UPPER bound.

The rotation-system (planar embedding) consistency test is applied only to the square-square subgraph, because the rotation at a wall node (the order of squares along that wall) is not determined by a decoration. Including the walls, and requiring the embedding to be consistent with the L4 drawing, would strengthen it further. It is measured by Monte Carlo, not enumerated.

Level-1 per-graph counts are exact; the per-k aggregate uses <= 160 sampled graphs, weighted by the MAIN count of their A-rep (reservoir sampling is uniform within an A-rep, so the estimator is unbiased across A-reps, but sampling error remains, especially in the max column).

Level 2 is extrapolation, not a bound. Three models are fitted to k=3..7 and the k=7 point is used as a one-step holdout for models fitted on k=3..6. The spread between models at k=11 is about a factor of 20.

Level 0 is exhaustive only for k = 3..7. Measured cost of k=8 with the present code is ~120 core-hours (5.3e11 mask rows); k >= 9 needs an orderly generator with metric pruning inside the generation, plus a canonical-labelling routine that does not enumerate k! permutations.

The brief's raw decoration menu (48 per square-square edge, 8 per square-wall edge) is an un-gauge-fixed encoding and is redundant non-uniformly. All decoration counts here are gauge-fixed (20 per SS edge, 2 per SW edge), where each label is one physically distinct arrangement.

Not used at all, and each would shrink the space: L5(c)-style strip capacity counts (soft), the A23/A25/A26 area-wastage ledger, A22-style local rigidity, the requirement that the FJ system of a structure actually has a solution with sigma <= s0, and any use of the known certified lower bound beyond the box endpoints.

findings: Level 0 is EXHAUSTIVE and orbit-exact for k = 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 (S_k x D4). MAIN hard survivors: k=3: 10, k=4: 140, k=5: 2275, k=6: 41951, k=7: 842398.

The survivor ratio N(k)/N(k-1) is close to LINEAR in k (3->4: 14.00, 4->5: 16.25, 5->6: 18.44, 6->7: 20.08), i.e. the space grows like k! times an exponential, not like a pure exponential. That is the shape that decides the campaign.

KEY STRUCTURAL FACT: the factorial-looking growth is entirely in the L2 THIN branch. The NON-THIN survivors (1, 19, 286, 4929, 88631) grow with an essentially CONSTANT ratio (19.0, 15.1, 17.2, 18.0), i.e. a pure exponential ~17^k, and all three fit models agree on their k=11 value to within 6% (~7e9). So if L2 degree-2 collinearity is upgraded from a thin branch to a hard prune, the structure space becomes exponential rather than factorial and the k=11 graph count drops by ~50x to ~7e9.

Filter strength (cumulative, orbit counts): the metric broad phase L5(a) is by far the strongest hard filter (k=7: 207791913 -> 4180697, x50), then L6 (x1.5) and full planarity (x3.3). L5(d) and the Euler bound are almost free.

Thin (L2 degree-2) branches are ~89% of MAIN at k=7; the two flagged branches that must be excluded by their own row systems are the lambda0=0 branch (401250, 48% of MAIN) and the L3 self-stress branch (871).

MAXWELL: not one survivor at any k reaches |E| >= 3k+1 (planarity caps |E| at 3k+2 and the observed maximum is {3: 7, 4: 10, 5: 13, 6: 16, 7: 20}). Every candidate structure therefore needs FLUSH contacts to be first-order rigid. If the Maxwell row count is ever proved necessary it becomes a very strong filter; the ledger currently marks it soft, so it is not applied.

A CERTIFIED tightening of L5(c) is available for free: two squares on the same wall have centres within sqrt2/2 of it and >= 1 apart, so their along-wall coordinates differ by >= 0.97832 while the range is s-1 <= 2.8771 - hence AT MOST 3 squares per wall, not 5. Applied as a soft column it keeps 623194 of 842398 MAIN survivors at k=7 (x0.74), and combined with dropping the L2 thin branches, 67130 (x13 smaller).

Level 1 (decorations): tilt propagation is exact for the tilt subsystem and kills 79.2%, 88.2%, 93.7%, 95.9%, 97.9% of the gauge-fixed menu at k=[3, 4, 5, 6, 7], but what survives still grows fast: weighted geometric-mean survivors per graph 271, 1.73e+04, 2.18e+06, 3.3e+08, 4.1e+10.

Level 1b: the ROTATION-SYSTEM (planar embedding) test that Level 1 ignores is a real filter and it strengthens fast with k. It removes 2%, 5%, 21%, 50% of the tilt-feasible decorations (weighted mean) at k=[4, 5, 6, 7], and for the MEDIAN graph it removes 0%, 0%, 51%, 91% - i.e. at k=7 a typical graph loses 91% of its decorations to embedding consistency alone. The weighted mean lags the median because a minority of low-degree graphs keep everything. This is the single cheapest unexploited constraint found here and it should be built into any structure-first generator; even so it does not change the order of magnitude of the k=11 projection.

PROJECTION to the full loaded core k=11 (extrapolation, not a bound): Level-0 graphs M1_exp 6.41e+10 / M2_logquad 5.02e+11 / M3_ratio_lin 3.43e+11; decoration fan-out ~6.5e+18; composed total M1_exp 4.15e+29 / M2_logquad 3.26e+30 / M3_ratio_lin 2.22e+30. Summed over all core sizes k=3..11 (rattler completion NOT counted): M1_exp 4.16e+29 / M2_logquad 3.26e+30 / M3_ratio_lin 2.22e+30.

BEST CASE if every cheap improvement lands (L2 promoted to a hard prune, the certified per-wall cap of 3 promoted, and the rotation-system test built into the decoration generator with its median keep-rate extrapolated to k=11, ~8e-04): about 4.9e+09 graphs x 5.2e+15 decorations = ~2.5e+25 structures at k=11. That is 5-6 orders of magnitude better than the naive count and still astronomically far beyond any compute budget - the verdict does not change.

GO/NO-GO: an enumerate-then-solve structure-first campaign at k=11 is not viable - ~1e11-1e12 contact graphs before decoration, ~1e30 decorated structures after. Even the undecorated Level-0 layer at 1 ms/graph is ~1e4 CPU-days. Viability requires (i) branching on structure jointly with the metric solve (prune during generation, never enumerate a level), (ii) promoting L2 and the certified per-wall cap 3 (about 1.5 orders of magnitude), and (iii) treating the contact TYPE (flush / corner-on-edge) as an algebraic unknown inside one FJ solve per graph rather than as 1e18 separate branches.
